headline: Big day for your ASX holdings — VGE surged 3.35% on a US-Iran peace deal that crushed oil prices, while the RBA meets this week with all four big banks tipping rates on hold.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a strong session today, jumping 3.35%. Emerging market shares got a big boost from the US-Iran peace deal — lower oil prices are great news for oil-importing emerging economies like India and China, which make up a large chunk of this ETF.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI climbed 2.58% today, riding continued enthusiasm for AI-related stocks on the ASX. The broader tech and AI theme remains strong globally, and this ETF is benefiting from that tailwind.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a solid session, up 1.34%. As a broadly diversified high-growth fund, it caught the wave of a strong ASX 200 day (up 1.25%) and positive global sentiment following the US-Iran deal.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained 1.09% today, reflecting last night's positive close on Wall Street where the S&P 500 rose 0.5%. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so it moves in line with American stocks.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG edged up 0.45% in last night's session. The stock is holding up ahead of Q2 earnings, though there's some noise about AI liability risks. The broader NASDAQ was fairly flat, so this was a quiet but positive night for Google.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: MSFT barely moved last night, up just 0.1%. The stock is under a bit of pressure from a class action lawsuit related to AI-linked losses, which is likely keeping a lid on gains even as the broader market ticked higher.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO slipped a tiny 0.16% in last night's session — essentially flat. The GTA 6 release is still on track for November according to reliable leakers, which is a key catalyst for this stock. Markets seem to be in a wait-and-see mode.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS dipped 0.61% today, a minor pullback despite some positive headlines around a lithium sector rebound and the commissioning of a new facility. Lithium prices remain depressed, which continues to weigh on the stock even with improving sentiment.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL was today's biggest loser in your portfolio, dropping 1.85%. The cause is clear — crude oil (WTI) crashed over 5% overnight after the US and Iran struck a peace deal, easing fears about Middle East supply disruptions. When oil prices fall sharply, energy company shares follow.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — Oil crashed 5%+ on US-Iran deal
watch_today.detail: Crude oil dropped from $84.88 to $80.50 overnight — a 5.16% fall — after the US and Iran reached a peace deal, which removed the fear premium (the extra price baked in due to supply-disruption risk) from oil markets. FUEL.AX fell 1.85% today as a result. If the deal holds, oil could stay lower for a while, which is a headwind for this ETF. Worth watching whether oil stabilises or keeps sliding.

watch_today.title: RBA meets this week — rates likely on hold
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia is meeting right now and is widely expected to keep the cash rate (the official interest rate it sets) on hold. All four of Australia's big banks agree. The AFR has run a contrarian piece arguing the market is wrong to assume the RBA is done — worth keeping in mind. A surprise rate move would jolt the ASX and your broader portfolio. Decision expected Tuesday.

watch_today.title: VGE.AX — Emerging markets surging, consider adding
watch_today.detail: VGE.AX jumped 3.35% today, its best session in a while. The US-Iran peace deal is a genuine tailwind for emerging market economies that import oil (think India, South Korea, Taiwan). Your position is tiny ($37 invested), so if you believe the deal holds and oil stays lower, this could be a decent spot to top up.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 November release confirmed by leaker
watch_today.detail: A well-known GTA leaker has stated GTA 6 will NOT miss its November 2026 release date. This is the biggest catalyst for Take-Two's share price — the game is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history. The stock is down 8.66% from your buy price, so patience is key here. If the release stays on track, the stock should re-rate significantly.

watch_today.title: GOOG — AI liability risk flagged ahead of Q2 earnings
watch_today.detail: Alphabet is up 23.9% from your cost base and ticking higher, but a new report flags growing AI liability risks heading into Q2 earnings. Nothing concrete yet, but worth keeping on your radar as earnings approach. For now the stock is performing well and the broader AI story remains intact.

watch_today.title: Gold hits record $4,336 — your VDHG benefits
watch_today.detail: Gold surged 2.88% overnight to $4,336 USD/oz — a striking new high. This reflects safe-haven demand (investors buying gold as a safety net) even as equities rally, suggesting some underlying nervousness in global markets. Gold's rise is a mild tailwind for VDHG which holds diversified assets.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a strong session today, up 1.25% to 8,914 — lifted by the US-Iran peace deal and a global risk-on mood. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 gained 0.5% and the NASDAQ edged up 0.31%. The big story in markets is oil, which crashed over 5% after the US and Iran struck a peace deal, removing Middle East supply fears. Gold surged to a new record above $4,336 USD/oz. The Aussie dollar ticked up slightly to 70.73 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong session today — lifted by global risk-on mood and the US-Iran peace deal.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session: modest gains on Wall Street as sentiment remains positive.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session: tech stocks edged higher but gains were modest.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Crashed over 5% overnight after the US-Iran peace deal reduced fears of Middle East supply disruptions.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Surged to a new record high — investors buying gold as a safety net even as equities rally.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar ticked slightly higher — traders feel a little more confident about global growth.

politics.summary: The big domestic story is the RBA meeting underway right now, with all signs pointing to rates staying on hold — though some analysts think the market is too complacent about future cuts. No other major Australian political stories broke today.

stories.title: RBA kicks off its June meeting — all big four banks tip rates on hold
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia started its June board meeting today, with ANZ, CBA, NAB, and Westpac all forecasting the cash rate will stay on hold. The rate has been on a downward path and markets are pricing in more cuts ahead — but the RBA hasn't committed to anything. The decision lands Tuesday. If you have a mortgage or are watching property markets, this is the one to follow.

stories.title: AFR contrarian view: 'Everyone thinks the RBA is done. They're wrong.'
stories.why_it_matters: The AFR is running a piece arguing the consensus view — that the RBA is basically finished cutting rates — is wrong. The argument is that inflation may prove stickier than expected, leaving rates higher for longer. No specific figures were available in the article text, but this is a minority view worth keeping in mind. If correct, it would be bad news for property prices and growth stocks.

stories.title: Prolonged pause on rates a possibility as RBA meets
stories.why_it_matters: The ABC reports that even if the RBA holds this week, the board may signal an extended pause — meaning no more rate cuts for a while — rather than giving the green light for further cuts. That would disappoint many mortgage holders hoping for relief sooner. The RBA has been careful not to pre-commit to a cutting path given ongoing uncertainty about inflation and the labour market.

ai.summary: The headline AI story today is the US government blocking Anthropic's latest Claude model — a significant move in the ongoing tug-of-war over AI regulation. Meanwhile, US states are fighting back against Trump's push to keep AI regulation at the federal level.

stories.title: US government shuts down Anthropic's latest Claude AI model
stories.why_it_matters: The US government has intervened to block Anthropic's newest version of its Claude AI model from being released or used — a rare and significant step. The article doesn't detail the specific model name or exact grounds, but this signals that US regulators are starting to actively block AI products they consider too risky. For investors in AI stocks (like your GXAI.AX ETF), this is a reminder that regulatory risk is real and growing — even in the US, which has generally been more hands-off than Europe.

stories.title: States press ahead with AI regulation despite Trump's push for federal control
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump has been pushing to keep AI regulation at the federal (national) level, which would likely mean lighter-touch rules. But several US states are ignoring that and pushing ahead with their own AI laws — similar to how California led the way on car emissions standards. This creates a patchwork of rules across the US, which makes compliance harder and more expensive for AI companies like Google (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT). It's a slow-burning headwind for the sector.

stories.title: Tyler Cowen: A Dangerous Turn in AI Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Economist Tyler Cowen has written a pointed piece arguing that recent moves to regulate AI — including government intervention in specific model releases — represent a dangerous shift. His concern is that heavy-handed regulation will slow innovation and hand an advantage to less-regulated rivals (read: China). The article text wasn't fully available, but Cowen is an influential voice and this adds to the broader debate about whether US AI policy is heading in the wrong direction.

stories.title: Get ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and more for life for $60
stories.why_it_matters: A $60 lifetime bundle for ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Claude, and other AI assistants is doing the rounds. It's a deal worth knowing about if you use any of these tools regularly — access to all the major AI assistants for a one-off payment rather than monthly subscriptions. The article doesn't specify which versions are included or the exact provider of the bundle, so read the fine print before buying.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 wrapped up with Jarome Luai starring in what turned out to be the final game ever at Leichhardt Oval. Round 16 fixtures are set for this weekend — including your Gold Coast Titans hosting the Panthers on Saturday arvo. AFL Round 14 coaches votes are in, and there's a minor storm over the AFL awards night outfits.

stories.title: Luai leads Tigers to historic final win at Leichhardt Oval
stories.why_it_matters: Jarome Luai was the star as Wests Tigers beat their opponent in what turned out to be the final NRL game ever played at Leichhardt Oval — the club's spiritual home ground. Fox Sports reports the Tigers have effectively admitted Luai is 'devastating' form, while the Eels face a halves dilemma after a shock rise from a rival. A bittersweet milestone for Tigers fans, but a win to savour.

stories.title: Round 16 team lists: Who's playing this weekend
stories.why_it_matters: Sporting News has published predicted team lists for all clubs heading into Round 16. Key local interest: the Gold Coast Titans host the Penrith Panthers on Saturday at 5:30pm at Cbus Super Stadium. Broncos, Eels, and Rabbitohs are all on the bye this week. Full team lists are out now if you want to check who's in and who's out before putting any tips in.

stories.title: Ex-Kangaroos winger eyeing NRL return; Walsh's back-up to earn new deal — Whispers
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports' NRL whispers column reports that a former Kangaroos (Australian national team) winger is eyeing a return to the NRL, and that Reece Walsh's back-up at the Broncos is set to be rewarded with a new contract. No specific names confirmed in the article text available, but transfer watch is heating up as clubs look ahead to next season.

stories.title: AFL Round 14 coaches votes in — Swans star makes big move
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL coaches votes for Round 14 are out, with five players earning perfect 10s from their opponents' coaches. A Sydney Swans player made a notable jump up the Brownlow (best-and-fairest award) leaderboard. The article doesn't name the Swans player without the full text, but it's shaping up as a competitive Brownlow race with multiple players in contention.
